slides.title: Reference Counting & Generational Garbage Collection
slides.prompt: CPython uses Reference Counting as its primary memory management mechanism. When an object's reference count drops to zero, its memory is deallocated immediately. Cyclic references are handled by CPython's generational Garbage Collector (gc module), which scans generations 0, 1, and 2.
slides.codeSnippet:
import sys
import gc

a = [1, 2, 3]
print(sys.getrefcount(a)) # Returns ref count + 1 (temporary ref from getrefcount)

# Cyclic reference
b = []
b.append(b)
gc.collect() # Manually triggers cyclic garbage collection

slides.title: Reference Count Decrease Trigger
slides.prompt: Which of the following operations DECREASES the reference count of an object in Python?

Passing the object as an argument to a function
Appending the object to a Python list
Assigning the object to a new alias variable
slides.correctAnswer: Reassigning or deleting (`del`) a variable name pointing to the object
